findings.text: the pointers-removed arm cites `r-20261105T091632392412-review-of-one-derivation-per-fact-82f3a3bdc63b`, and no such run directory exists under `~/.config/reckon/crew/runs/` (checked: a promoted control, `r-20261103T072523194588-measure-what-a-nodes-time-budget-controls-and-how-much-of-it`, does keep its directory, and 5021 run directories are present), so a reader cannot check the only evidence for that arm

findings.reason: an arm with no negative control measures nothing, and the two newest arms are the only ones covering the manifest-overwrite loss the section now claims.
findings.text: the second case asserts three outcomes (a held request is not launched, a pointer-removed request is not launched, a request whose run has an attempt that already exited with a result is not launched), while the two stated negative controls — the admission lock in `hold` making the first case time out, and removing the pre-launch phase re-read making the held arm launch — falsify only the held arm, so nothing shows the other two arms can fail and a node implementing only the held guard passes the case

findings.reason: a worker implementing the Deliverable as written cannot satisfy its own Done when's third arm, and will either fail the gate or invent an unstated mechanism.
findings.text: the Deliverable's mechanism is "re-reads its phase under the pointer write just before it launches", which detects a hold and (via the missing pointer) a removal, but not a run whose earlier attempt already exited with a result: the cited instance shows the first attempt exiting at 12:00:46Z and a relaunch at 12:08:10Z under the same run id, and the run's record carries `attempt-1-exit.json` and `attempt-1-review-filed.json` beside the pointer, so the guard the arm needs must consult the recorded attempt, a source the Deliverable never names

findings.reason: the section cannot be closed on one verdict, and it is the second repair whose controls are missing, so splitting it is exactly what would surface them.
findings.text: §35 now carries two independent repairs: `hold`/`release` leaving `_admit_lock` (`reckon/crew/queue_edit.py:594,613`), and a launch-time staleness check in `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py` whose arms (pointer removed by promotion/discard/drop; an attempt already exited with a result, overwriting a delivered manifest) share no code, no root cause and no evidence with the lock
